marks.gloss_en: והרי תפלה דדבר שהצבור עסוקין בו, ותנן: היה עומד בתפלה ונזכר שהוא בעל קרי לא יפסיק אלא יקצר -- טעמא דאתחיל, הא לא אתחיל לא יתחיל! -- prayer too is what the community is engaged in, yet a baal keri who has not begun may not begin
the mishnah (22b): one standing in prayer who remembers he is a baal keri does not stop, but abridges
אלא: קריאת שמע וברכת המזון דאורייתא, ותפלה דרבנן (= p_krishma_deoraita, p_bhm_deoraita, p_tefilla_derabanan)
והרי ברכת המזון לאחריו דלית בה מלכות שמים, ותנן: על המזון מברך לאחריו ואינו מברך לפניו! -- Birkat HaMazon also lacks the kingship of Heaven, yet the baal keri says it
the stam's first answer: prayer is different, for it has no [acceptance of the] kingship of Heaven
food requires no blessing before yet requires one after; Torah, which requires one before, surely requires one after
Torah requires no blessing after yet requires one before; food, which requires one after, surely requires one before
מה למזון שכן נהנה -- what of food? there he derives bodily benefit, which Torah study does not share
מה לתורה שכן חיי עולם -- what of Torah? it is eternal life, which food does not share
the blessing after food is from the Torah -- 'and you shall eat and be satisfied and bless'
the blessing before Torah study is from the Torah -- 'when I proclaim the name of the Lord, ascribe greatness to our God'
one who prayed, entered the synagogue and found the congregation praying: if he can introduce something new in it, he prays again

had he taught us the first [ruling], [one would say] that holds of individual and individual or congregation and congregation, but an individual vis-a-vis the congregation is as one who has not prayed -- so he taught us [this one]

איני?! והאמר רב נחמן... גומרין כל אותה ברכה -- one who erred on Shabbat completes the whole blessing; how then does one stop in the middle of a blessing? (kind svara under protest: no ObjectionKind for an amoraic-memra contradiction)
one who was standing in prayer and remembered that he had already prayed stops -- even in the middle of a blessing
הכי השתא! there the man is obligated and only the Rabbis spared him because of the honour of Shabbat; here he has already prayed (= p_hatam_bar_chiyuva, p_lo_atrechuhu_kvod_shabbat)
there the man is one who is obligated [in the prayer]; but here he has already prayed
מאי טעמא? ... אמת ויציב דאורייתא -- the reason one in doubt says Emet veYatziv again is that it is Torah law
one in doubt whether he recited the Shema recites it again -- denied by Rav Yehuda (אינו חוזר וקורא), asserted by R' Elazar
מתיב רב יוסף: ובשכבך ובקומך -- the Torah itself commands reciting at lying down and rising
אמר ליה אביי: ההוא בדברי תורה כתיב -- that verse is written of words of Torah
'and when you lie down and when you rise' (Deut 6:7)
תנן: בעל קרי... ואינו מברך לא לפניה ולא לאחריה; ואי סלקא דעתך אמת ויציב דאורייתא -- לברוך לאחריה! -- were it Torah law, the baal keri would say the blessing after the Shema
מאי טעמא מברך? אי משום יציאת מצרים -- הא אדכר ליה בקריאת שמע (= p_adkar_bekrishma)
the stam: if [Emet veYatziv] is said because of the Exodus, the Exodus is already mentioned in the Shema
ונימא הא ולא ליבעי הא! -- then let him say this [Emet veYatziv] and not need that [the Shema]
קריאת שמע עדיפא, דאית בה תרתי -- the Shema is preferable, for it has two things
one in doubt whether he prayed prays again -- the proposition R' Elazar denies
